newsitem.title: POLAND: Demand for Polish 3-yr T-bonds seen matching offer.
newsitem.headline: Demand for Polish 3-yr T-bonds seen matching offer.

text.p: Polish three-year floating Treasury bonds are expected to attract around 250 to 350 million zlotys ($100.8 million) demand against the finance ministry's 300 million zloty offer, dealers said on Tuesday.
The T-bond auction will be on Wednesday.

"Demand will mainly come from the outside of the banking sector, with most bids placed by insurance companies and corporates, and foreign investors virtually absent," said Marcin Rzechowski, fixed income dealer at Societe Generale.
Dealers said the floating bonds linked to 13-week T-bill yields were a good long-term investment due to rising T-bill yields.
But they said the bonds were unattractive for speculative trading because they lacked liquidity.
"Firms should be interested in three-year bonds as this is a good investment when the T-bill yields are on the rise, but they are not liquid," said Marta Muscinska, bond dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
